messages:
Maya Chen: Hey team — quick week0 sync for Ginkgo Labs (acct: ginkgo-prod). Two blockers from their security review: KMS key grant and audit log forwarding. Alex, do you have the CMK created with the cross-account policy we asked for?
Alex M. (Ginkgo): Yep, CMK is created in our account. I applied a grant to allow Redwood's service principal but I wasn't 100% sure about the exact ARN you needed. I can paste policy if that helps.
Maya Chen: Please paste it. We need to confirm the KeyPolicy allows the Redwood KMS role and that the grant includes Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. If not, we risk delay >1 week which bumps renewal conversation to red. :warning:
Alex M. (Ginkgo): Paste below:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwood",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-kms-role" },
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Leo Park: That looks close. Two notes: 1) KeyPolicy shouldn't rely only on role ARN; prefer a condition on aws:SourceAccount and include the service principal used by our private connectors. 2) We'll need a grant ID if you want us to rotate keys without interruption. I'll DM the exact role/service principal strings. :eyes:
Priya Desai: Also check audit logs. We need either S3 bucket + KMS encryption (same CMK) OR a Cross-Account CloudWatch Logs subscription to our ingest account. Which are you leaning toward? The compliance team requires immutable logs for 90 days.
Alex M. (Ginkgo): Their infra team prefers S3 with lifecycle. I can set up a bucket and give you write perms. Question: should logs be encrypted with that same CMK or a separate archival key?
Maya Chen: Prefer same CMK to simplify access control, but if your security wants a separate archival key we can map that in the RBAC. As long as Redwood's ingest principal can PutObject and PutObjectAcl to the bucket. Example bucket policy we need: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-logs-writer"},
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject","s3:PutObjectAcl"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::ginkgo-redwood-logs/*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Alex M. (Ginkgo): I'll provision the bucket and attach that policy. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Priya Desai: Great — one more: we need the IAM assume-role trust policy for the role Redwood will use to pull logs/ship. Please include the external ID we provided.
Leo Park: I'll prepare the exact trust JSON and upload to the onboarding doc. Also tagging ticket #CS-842 for auditability.
Maya Chen: Action items: 1) Alex to share final CMK ARN + confirm grant ID (due EOD tomorrow). 2) Alex to create S3 bucket with policy (EOD tomorrow). 3) Leo to post trust policy + external-id (today). 4) Priya to validate audit retention & immutability controls (by Fri). If any of these slip, call me — this is the gating item for Private deployment go/no-go and impacts their renewal risk.
deploy-bot: Audit shipper lambda test invoked successfully for ginkgo-redwood-logs (test-id: d3f5a9).
Alex M. (Ginkgo): Thanks — I'll update the shared doc with ARNs and bucket name in ~6h.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. Quick note for enablement: schedule a 30m runbook walk-through with Ginkgo next Tue so Support can reproduce restores. I'll send calendar invite. :thumbsup:
